description.narrative: The most significant expected project-level outcome is an increased access to finance for agri-MSMEs, including agri-WMSMEs (Women-owned MSMEs). Agricultural finance remains severely constrained in Senegal. Most formal financial institutions view the sector as high-risk due to challenges such as income variability, poor collateral frameworks, weather-related risks, and limited availability of financial data. These constraints are especially pronounced among female entrepreneurs, who have more limited access to bank financing than their male counterparts. Beyond the project-level outcomes, IFC anticipates that this Project will promote greater market resilience of Senegals agricultural value chain via the demonstration and replication channels, serving as proof of the commercial viability of lending to the agricultural sector.

The proposed Project aims to support a Senegalese microfinance institution, Union des Mutuelles du Partenariat pour la Mobilisation de lÉpargne et du Crédit Au Sénégal (PAMECAS or the MFI), with an agricultural risk sharing facility (RSF) of up to US$7 million equivalent whereby IFC will guarantee up to 70 percent of an up to US$10 million equivalent portfolio of eligible loans from smallholder farmers, cooperatives and agri micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The investment will be tranched with the first tranche covering a c.US$1 million portfolio, with up to US$0.7m loss coverage.
